chapter: Learning the trombone and jam sessions
title: Lineup of the Dick Gibson jazz party
summary: He lists the trombones, trumpets, saxophones and rhythm players and reads out how Gibson boxes the sets.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Did you play with Watrous and Rosolino (unintelligible) this year at Dick Gibson's?
Not this year. Last year I did. Al Grey played with them this year. But last year I played with them.
Who'd you play with this year?

I played with Al Grey and I played with Vic. We played together. And there's another guy up there that plays with the World's Greatest Jazz Band now, George Masso. He's a good trombone player. I played with George. And I really enjoyed it, you know. It was fun. It was a fun thing. It got to cooking up there because they had a lot of good rhythm players up there.
Who else was there this year? I didn't see the Lineup (inaudible)...

Well, the trombones was -- were Watrous, Rosolino, Carl Fontana, Vic Dickinson, myself, Al Grey, George Masso. And the trumpets were -- trumpets were Clark Terry, and Ruby Braff, Pee Wee Erwin, Joe Wilder, and Jon

Fattis, somebody else. There's so many -- there were 51 guys up there, you know. And a lot of saxophone players. Zoot Sims, Al Cohn, Budd Johnson, Benny Carter. I know I'm leaving some out. Phil Woods. There's some amazing guys up there. And Buddy DeFranco was up there. And Buddy Tate. And what's that guy who used to arrange for Basie? Tenor man. Ernie Wilkins.

A lot of good -- it's hard to sit right down and think of all of them, but there's so many good players up there. It was a fun thing, you know. And they had a lot of drummers, lot of piano players, lot of bass players. Ray Brown, Red Callender, Ted Galner, Milt Hinton, Major Holley. And what's the little young bass player around New York, plays real good.

No. This guy teaches. He went to the University of Indiana. What was his name? What's his name, Sally? Oh, here's the list. Help me out. (unintelligible) -- some of the sets like it would be Bucky Pizzarelli, Herb Ellis, Phil Woods, Roger Calloway, George Duvivier, and Roland Hanna -- no Jake Hanna. That was one set. That set went on 12:00. This is Monday afternoon, 12:00 to 8:30. 12:35 Bill Watrous, Zoot Sims, Budd Johnson, Ernie Wilkins, Buddy DeFranco, Roland Hanna, Red Callender, Alan Dawson. The third set went

on 1:05 to 1:40 was Pee Wee Irwin, myself, Flip Phillips, Bob Holley, Bob Leeman. Wilber, Dave McKenna, Major Harle, Cliff Leeman. 1:40, the set was Faddis -- John Faddis, Carl Fontana, Phil Woods, Al Flanagan, Tommy Flannigan, Ridley -- Larry Ridley -- that's the guy I was trying to think of.

Roy Haynes, and Herb Ellis. Then 2:20 was Ruby Braff, Al Gray, George Masso, Buddy Tate, and Jerry Fuller, Ralph Sutton, Ray Brown, Panama Francis. These are just sets. In every box you see 15 the soloist for that set -- they featured solos for different sets. And these are all different sets. But it was fun. It was a fun thing.

This is how he makes his sets out. See, he box in the sets. I -- it's Sunday afternoon -- these are the things -- the different things that go on. And Dick makes the sets out. They're beautiful the way he did -- does, and it sure works. I guess I'm runnig my mouth on this stuff. I -- No -- it was interesting.
